structure_cache_spec.ragged_support_note: The zb axis is DELIBERATELY ragged: ocean nodes cannot populate zb above ~45 km and frozen nodes cannot populate below ~47 km. Nodes unbuildable on both branches store None and leave support, per the Titan precedent. REVIEWER RULING 2026-08-13 — PARTIALLY RATIFIED: the ragged axis is ratified FOR THE BUILD (the ocean-branch posterior is provably undistorted: a uniform prior on [5,70] restricted to the ocean sub-interval is, after normalization, identical to a uniform prior on [5,45]) — CONDITIONAL on unbuildable nodes contributing exactly -inf log-likelihood with NO nearest-node fallback across a None, which must be tested. But the BRANCH-MASS RATIO is NOT ratified as drawn: see branch_mass_reporting_ruling.
structure_cache_spec.branch_mass_reporting_ruling: REQUIRED (reviewer, declined to ratify the continuous-prior version). On the frozen branch zb is NOT a free parameter: at fixed rho_ice, mass conservation makes zb <-> rho_rock a bijection (47.5 / 57.2 / 65.3 / 70.2 km at rho_rock 2200 / 2400 / 2600 / 2741). So the frozen branch has 4 free dimensions, not 5, and its prior mass — 35.4% of the box as drawn — is set ENTIRELY BY WHERE THE UPPER EDGE SITS: move hi from 70 to 80 km and frozen prior mass becomes ~44%; drop to 60 and it becomes ~21%. The reported ocean/no-ocean odds would then be linearly rescalable by an arbitrary box edge — precisely the fragile statistic the NH3 C16 saga identified (project_joint_mixture_gate_scope / the §0.20-§0.21 branch-mass work). The VERDICT survives regardless (the frozen branch is discriminated at tens of sigma, so the odds are astronomically one-sided), but the NUMBER is not interpretable. FIX: report the branch comparison as an EXPLICIT DISCRETE MODEL INDEX with declared prior odds (P(ocean) = P(frozen) = 0.5), computing each branch's evidence over its own support; and state in the config that on the frozen branch zb_km is a deterministic reparameterization of rock density, so a 'frozen-branch posterior on zb' is read as a posterior on rho_rock.
structure_cache_spec.frozen_rock_density_prior_now_implicit: Reviewer sub-finding (ii)/(iii): d(rho_rock)/d(zb) ~ 22-28 kg m^-3 km^-1 over 47-70 km, so zb ~ U[47,70] induces an approximately uniform rho_rock over ~[2196, 2741] — a defensible range with the H&M/Park 2340-2410 band interior. The problem is that it is now UNDECLARED: CRITICAL-1 removed rho_core_kgm3 ~ U[2200,2600], which was the only declared bound on rock density, so the frozen branch's density prior is implicit in a box edge. Either restore a declared rho_rock range for the frozen branch or state the induced prior explicitly. Interacts with the mass-conservation invariant above.

mandatory_node_invariants.mass_conservation: QUADRATURE IS PART OF THE SPECIFICATION (fixed 2026-08-13, reviewer NEW-CRITICAL-1). Compute M_node with MIDPOINT-EDGE shells: edges = [0, (r_i + r_{i+1})/2 ..., r_last]; M = sum(rho_i * 4/3 pi (edge_{i+1}^3 - edge_i^3)). Require abs(M_node / M_body - 1) < 5e-4. HARD REJECT to None on failure.
mandatory_node_invariants.zb_placement: abs(zb_km_actual - zb_km_node) < grid_step_km / 2. HARD REJECT to None on failure.
mandatory_node_invariants.why_blocking: Reviewer MAJOR-1, reproduced by Machine B against the existing smoke cache (PlanetProfile/Test/mcmc_results/Enceladus/Cassini_smoke/enceladus_seawater_smoke_grid.pkl): integrating each node's own profile gives a mass DEFICIT of -22.16% (node 0, Tb=271.8, frozen, phases {1,50}) and -9.21% (node 1, Tb=272.1, frozen) against -0.31% (node 2, Tb=272.46, the only OCEAN node — numerical). All three nodes store Mtot_kg = 1.08022e20, the template constant, so the stored field MASKS the violation entirely. PP built and persisted the violating frozen nodes without complaint. Two consequences: (1) this config's earlier claim that interior density is 'recoverable as a DERIVED display quantity from the cache via mass conservation' is FALSE ON THE FROZEN BRANCH — deriving rho_interior from Mtot_kg minus the hydrosphere would be wrong by tens of percent, and that claim was load-bearing for the CRITICAL-1 core-parameter drop; (2) widening the zb box to 70 km does NOT fix this by itself, because the builder rejects mass-violating frozen nodes at NO zb. Without the zb_placement invariant a frozen retry requested at zb=20 but built by PP at zb_actual~47 would be stored with theta and structure disagreeing by 27 km, silently corrupting the likelihood. Suspected mechanism (reviewer, medium confidence): PP matches MoI or PHydroMax rather than mass on the NO_OCEAN_EXCEPT_INNER_ICES path. MUST be root-caused before B4, and the smoke cache's frozen nodes must be re-audited or discarded.
mandatory_node_invariants.mass_conservation_why_the_quadrature_mat: The first version of this invariant said only '< 1e-3 from the node's own (r_m, rho) arrays' and did NOT name the quadrature. That was UNIMPLEMENTABLE and would have emptied the cache of the ocean branch. r_m is the OUTER bound of each layer (defineStructs.py), so the natural layer-top reading assigns rho[i] to [r[i-1], r[i]] — and measured on the smoke cache that puts the ONLY physically-sound node (node 2, the ocean node) at 0.3118%, a hard reject against a 0.1% threshold, while the two mass-VIOLATING frozen nodes are at -22.16% and -9.21%. Machine B reproduced all three quadratures: layer_top -22.1582 / -9.2112 / -0.3118 %; trapezoid on 4 pi r^2 rho -21.8422 / -8.8465 / -0.0057 %; midpoint-edge -21.8482 / -8.8567 / -0.0182 %. The ocean node's apparent 0.3118% is pure shell-attribution error, not physics — the profile is internally consistent to ~2e-4. Midpoint-edge is chosen over trapezoid because it closes the total volume EXACTLY by construction (verified: +2.2e-14%), so the residual measures density inconsistency alone. Threshold 5e-4 is set from the measured good-node baseline (1.8e-4) with ~3x headroom, and it still rejects both frozen nodes by >100x.
mandatory_node_invariants.acceptance_criteria_BOTH_DIRECTIONS: The invariant test MUST FAIL on smoke nodes 0 and 1 AND MUST PASS on smoke node 2. The earlier requirement stated only the FAIL half, which is exactly why the empty-cache defect slipped through. A one-sided acceptance criterion for a rejection rule is not a test.
mandatory_node_invariants.branch_flag_source: has_ocean MUST be derived from the PHASE ARRAY (presence of any phase-0 liquid layer), NEVER from D_ocean_km. Verified 2026-08-13 (reviewer NEW-MINOR-3): smoke nodes 0 and 1 store D_ocean_km = 1.510 and 1.151 km while having NO phase-0 layers at all, so a D_ocean_km > 0 test would misclassify frozen nodes as ocean — and the discrete branch index depends on that classification.

structure_cache_spec.w_axis_scope: The log10_w axis applies to the OCEAN branch only. Frozen nodes have no ocean, so salinity is undefined there (not merely unconstrained) and the frozen segment is built at a single nominal w with w recorded as N/A. Node count above is therefore an upper bound; the builder must not multiply frozen zb nodes by 40 salinities.
